messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's rollout gating tweak we see a p99 drift in the console latency pane for a subset of endpoints. Not huge, but reproducible across cohorts.
liam: which gating tweak? the fallback weight change for low-tier routes?
maria: yeah, reduced primary weight and increased fallback to keep throughput steady. p50/p95 mostly unchanged. p99 jumps ~200ms for endpoints hitting fallback.
sasha: can you paste the query slice? is this by-route or by-client?
maria: by-route + cache_hit tag. here's the snippet I used in the dashboard query:
```
SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
FROM latency_events
WHERE route IN ('/v1/generate','/v1/chat')
AND ts >= now() - interval '30m'
GROUP BY route, cache_hit
```
liam: interesting. cache_hit=false has the jump?
maria: exactly. cache_hit=true stays flat. Also more pronounced for long-seq workloads.
rachel: could sampling bias from rollout gating be amplifying tail values? if fallback serves a different model variant or cold KV cache, tails would worsen.
sasha: rollout policy made fallback weight explicit (0.3 -> 0.6). fallback runs on smaller instances + no local kvcache. that matches cache_hit=false + heavier tails.
liam: ops-bot: can you confirm whether those fallback nodes had a config change last night?
ops-bot: deploy-log: fallback-pool v2.4 rolled at 6773180000 by deployer. no other config changes noted.
liam: thanks. hypothesis: more requests routed to fallback -> higher cold-kv miss rate -> heavier tail. two mitigation paths: (1) adjust sampling shown in console to annotate provenance (primary vs fallback) and surface p99 by origin; (2) change sampling for percentile computation to weight by origin counts so p99 isn't suddenly dominated by a small noisy pool.
maria: +1 on provenance annotation. For (2) we currently compute percentile over raw events. weight-by-origin sounds tricky — would change SLO semantics.
sasha: agree. We should avoid changing definition of p99 SLOs. Instead add a dashboard decomposition column: p50/p95/p99 per origin (primary/fallback/edge) and show sample counts. UX: a small pill next to percentile shows origin breakdown on hover.
rachel: we also need to surface sample size and min sample threshold. this was noisy: fallback had ~120 samples which is borderline for p99.
liam: pragmatic short-term: add a telemetry rule to emit an alert when p99 delta > 100ms AND origin concentration > 40% from a single origin with sample_count < 500. that avoids noisy alerts for tiny pools.
maria: can someone draft the alert rule? I can add the dashboard widgets.
sasha: I'll draft the alert. Proposed pseudo-rule:
```
if (p99_total - p99_primary) > 100ms && (count_from_single_origin / total_count) > 0.4 && total_count < 500:
  alert("p99-origin-concentration")
```
liam: minor nit: total_count < 500 will suppress large-volume incidents; we probably want OR total_count < X depending on signal. but good start.
ops-bot: note: fallback pool v2.4 has increased cold-kv misses logged. trace id sample: trace-9a3f.
maria: OK next steps: sasha will open alert PR, I will add a breakdown card to the console route latency panel (per-origin p50/p95/p99 + counts), liam please coordinate with infra to check fallback kvcache warming config.
liam: on it. I'll check warm-start config and look for options to pre-warm kvcache on rollover.
rachel: for longer term we should consider showing p99 stratified by inference_variant and cache_hit by default for any rollout > 10% weight to fallback.
sasha: noted. will include that in the UX doc.
maria: thanks all. tagging @dev-bot to create a checklist task.
dev-bot: task created: "dashboard: add origin decomposition and sample count for latency panel" assigned to maria, link: https://issues/internal/INF-2345 :thumbsup:
liam: thanks. keeping this thread for coordination. feel free to ping me if you need logs/traces.
maria: done — added initial card draft in the console staging workspace. inviting reviewers.
